chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'How beautiful are the good deeds after the evil deeds, and how ugly are the evil deeds after the good deeds.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of good deeds following evil deeds in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elucidates the spiritual dynamics of moral consistency, emphasizing that the beauty of good deeds is amplified when they follow sins, as they demonstrate sincere repentance and struggle (mujahada). Conversely, sins committed after a period of righteousness are considered more ugly because they represent a fall from a higher station of awareness. This teaching underscores the Shia scholarly view that the journey of the believer is often defined by the resilience of returning to God after failure, rather than static perfection.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoubm from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘How good are the good deeds after the evil deeds, and how ugly are the evil deeds after the good deeds’.
en.sarwar: 18. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub from abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I heard abu Ja’far (a.s.) saying ‘
How excellent are good deeds after evil deeds and how disgraceful are evil deeds after good deeds!”’
